facts.claim: Inferences of competence based solely on facial appearance predicted the outcomes of U.S. congressional elections better than chance (e.g., 68.8% of the Senate races in 2004).
facts.quote: We show that inferences of competence based solely on facial appearance predicted the outcomes of U.S. congressional elections better than chance (e.g., 68.8% of the Senate races in 2004)

facts.claim: Once learned, first impressions occur following very brief exposure (100 ms).
facts.quote: Crucially, in the final two experiments (Experiments 4 and 5) we show that, once learned, these first impressions occur following very brief exposure (100 ms).

facts.claim: Judgments made after a 100-ms exposure to a face correlated highly with judgments made in the absence of time constraints.
facts.quote: Judgments made after a 100-ms exposure correlated highly with judgments made in the absence of time constraints, suggesting that this exposure time was sufficient for participants to form an impression.

facts.claim: Trait impressions from voices require longer exposure to develop and stabilize although they are still formed by 400 ms.
facts.quote: Unlike faces, however, trait impressions from voices require longer exposure to develop and stabilize although they are still formed by 400 ms.

facts.claim: When exposure time increased from 100 to 500 ms, participants' judgments became more negative, response times for judgments decreased, and confidence in judgments increased.
facts.quote: When exposure time increased from 100 to 500 ms, participants' judgments became more negative, response times for judgments decreased, and confidence in judgments increased.

research.angle: People form trait impressions from faces in as little as 100 milliseconds, though these impressions can be learned and may differ from those formed from voices.
research.verdict: The evidence confirms that trait inferences from faces occur rapidly, often within 100 milliseconds, and can influence real-world behaviors like voting.
research.caveat: While impressions are formed rapidly, increasing exposure time can lead to more negative judgments and more differentiated person impressions.
